findings.reason: A REVERSE wrist curl is wrist extension. The row stores forearm_flexors as primary plus biceps_brachii_long primary and brachialis secondary, i.e. the muscle set of an elbow-flexion curl. forearm_extensors exists in the muscle vocabulary and is absent.

The 'twist' of a twisting dumbbell bench press is forearm rotation, not trunk rotation. Both obliques are stored as secondary movers and the only stored joint action is spine:rotation, which no bench press performs.

Both pectoralis heads and the anterior deltoid are stored as secondary movers of a dumbbell biceps curl; only the elbow flexors act. The row also carries shoulder:horizontal_adduction and scapula:protraction as joint actions and horizontal_press as its primary pattern.

The description is a seated incline front raise. Serratus anterior is stored as a PRIMARY mover although it is a scapular protractor and no scapular action is stored; the movers are the deltoid heads.

Latissimus dorsi is stored as a PRIMARY mover of a prone incline Y-raise; the lat extends and adducts the shoulder and is the direct antagonist of the movement. The stored joint action is also shoulder:adduction, the opposite of the raise.

A seated barbell wrist curl is pure wrist flexion with the forearms braced on the thighs; biceps brachii long is stored as a primary mover and brachialis as secondary, and the stored joint action is elbow:flexion instead of wrist:flexion.

In a lateral raise the prime mover is the LATERAL deltoid, stored here only as secondary, while deltoid_anterior and trapezius_middle are primary and triceps_brachii_long is stored as a secondary mover of a straight-arm raise.
Battle ropes are an inertial rope, not a hydraulic device. The only linked equipment is cable_attachment_rope, a cable handle rather than a battle rope.
A close-grip push-up off dumbbells carries no external load; the row already stores bodyweight_leverage, bodyweight_reps and bodyweight_aware, all of which contradict bodyweight=false.

The exercise is named and described as targeting the posterior deltoid, yet deltoid_ANTERIOR is stored as primary with placeholder low/low/low tension and deltoid_posterior only as secondary. The anterior head is the antagonist of the stored joint action shoulder:horizontal_abduction.

Same inversion as the dumbbell version: deltoid_anterior is primary on an exercise whose stored joint action is shoulder:horizontal_abduction, for which it is the antagonist, and deltoid_posterior is demoted to secondary with placeholder tension.
A reverse fly is shoulder horizontal abduction. Deltoid_anterior, a horizontal ADDuctor, and latissimus dorsi are stored as the two primaries while deltoid_posterior is only secondary.

The profile is bodyweight_plus_weight / added_weight / bodyweight_aware with bodyweight_leverage resistance, and the comparable loaded-bodyweight entries in the same sample (chin_up, ring_muscle_up) store bodyweight=true.

In a SEATED calf raise the knee is flexed, so the gastrocnemius is slack and the soleus is the prime mover. The row stores gastrocnemius_lateral as primary with placeholder low/low/low tension and soleus as secondary; tibialis anterior, the antagonist, is stored as a stabilizer with high/high tension.
A rear lunge loads one leg at a time with the other leg behind; every comparable split-stance entry is unilateral, and side_mode is already 'optional', which only makes sense for a per-side movement.

A head harness loaded by a hanging plate is not a cam machine, and the linked equipment is back_extension_machine, a machine the exercise does not use.

The exercise stores bodyweight=true and has no equipment linked, but the profile is bodyweight_plus_weight / added_weight, implying an external load that does not exist.

findings.proposed: remove deltoid_anterior; keep latissimus_dorsi and teres_major as primary
findings.reason: The stored primary joint action is shoulder:extension, and deltoid_anterior - a shoulder flexor and therefore the antagonist - is stored as one of the primary movers.
